sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Stonecrest, Georgia?
sections.html:
Selling in Stonecrest can go three ways: an agent markets the house, you market it yourself, or an investor pays cash and absorbs the repairs. The size of the repair list, what you still owe, your deadline and who lives inside will tip the decision.

  • Agents suit houses that show well and owners who are not in a hurry.
  • Selling yourself drops the commission and leaves price, disclosures and haggling to you.
  • Cash bids are worth requesting for a house with deferred repairs, back taxes or an estate behind it.

Stonecrest lies within DeKalb County, so county tax offices handle every parcel here, while the city keeps its own permit and licensing staff.

sections.h2: What is Stonecrest, and how new is the city?
sections.html:
Few Georgia cities are as new. Residents voted for incorporation on November 8, 2016, and city government opened for business on July 10, 2017, as the city's 2020 financial report records. The report ranked Stonecrest sixteenth in size among the state's cities in 2020 and called it primarily a bedroom community of roughly 29 square miles.

City staff handle planning and zoning, code enforcement, business licenses, and building permits and inspections. DeKalb County kept police, fire, road maintenance and sanitation during the transition, and the report says the county still supplies public safety. Five council members chosen by district sit beside a mayor, and in 2020 the city activated an Urban Redevelopment Agency that issued revenue bonds to buy land and buildings for city use. The report adds that the city first assessed a millage rate in 2020, modeled on a proposed DeKalb parks and recreation millage, and that franchise taxes, business taxes and permit fees cover most other services. Ask the DeKalb Tax Commissioner how any city levy appears on your bill.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Stonecrest housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate puts Stonecrest at 61,337 people, 3.6 percent above the 2020 base, in 20,995 households. Owners occupy 56.3 percent of the homes.

A landlord-minded buyer will weigh a house against that $1,601 rent. The 36 minute average commute is long, which squares with the city's own bedroom community label.

sections.h2: What makes Stonecrest different from other DeKalb County addresses?
sections.html:
The city's 2020 report names the Mall at Stonecrest as the commercial hub, ringed by medical, office and hotel parcels, with DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale as the main hospital. It also identifies two industrial areas that host some of the biggest local employers, including Dart Container and Home Chef.

The same report places the city near Interstate 20 and State Routes 124 and 278, which lead toward downtown Atlanta and Hartsfield-Jackson airport. Its 2020 list of principal employers also includes Trojan Battery, Plaid Enterprise, Griffith Foods and the DeKalb Medical Center at Hillandale, so a house here draws workers from several fields.

The outdoor side is just as distinctive. The Arabia Mountain National Heritage Area covers 2,550 acres of exposed granite, wetlands, streams, lakes and forest, linked by a trail network, and the Davidson-Arabia Mountain Nature Park and Panola Mountain State Park add to that. The city's tourism page points to the historic Flatrock community and to African American history and arts as parts of its visitor story.

For a seller, these places are selling points. A house near the heritage area trails or close to the mall corridor can be described by its distance to them, and a buyer who works at the industrial parks may value a short drive.

sections.h2: When are DeKalb County property taxes due, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
DeKalb's August bills name the January 1 owner, with a second mailing for a different current owner. Payment can be split between September 30 and November 15, or made in full by September 30. A mailed check needs a hand-canceled post office postmark by the date, and the county does not accept metered or kiosk postage as proof of timely mailing. Missing the date adds a 5 percent penalty.

If the deed moved after January 1, the tax commissioner's page points the new owner toward the closing statement, the attorney, the lender or the escrow agent for an answer on who pays. Whatever goes unpaid keeps accruing against the parcel. The county does not mail bills to lenders, which is why a seller on escrow should confirm the money was sent.

On a single-family home the county prints the yearly sanitation assessment, for trash pickup, as $362.30.

sections.h2: How do DeKalb homestead exemptions and appeals work?
sections.html:
The county's brochure lays out the DeKalb homestead tests: occupy the house as your primary home on January 1, hold a Georgia license or ID with the address, and keep your vehicles registered there. Filing closes in mid-July. Exemptions are never automatic and never pass to a buyer. Once granted, an exemption puts an assessment freeze on county taxes that may limit an increase, though it leaves school, city and state taxes alone.

  • Income-tested special exemptions go to residents 62 and older, disabled residents, 100 percent disabled veterans and certain surviving spouses.
  • An appeal has 45 days from the notice, and the county refuses anything sent by fax or email.
  • Owners choose among the Board of Equalization at no charge, nonbinding arbitration for $217 plus a certified appraisal, or a hearing officer for non-homestead property valued over $500,000.
  • If your appeal is unresolved when bills print, you are billed on a temporary value, typically the smaller of last year's final value or 85 percent of this year's.

Property is appraised at 100 percent of fair market value and assessed at 40 percent. The Property Appraisal Department is at 325 Swanton Way in Decatur, and the Tax Commissioner's central office is at 4380 Memorial Drive in Decatur.

sections.h2: What do transfer tax and recording involve in Stonecrest?
sections.html:
Georgia holds back a deed from the records until the transfer tax is in. The seller is liable unless the contract says otherwise, and the Department of Revenue's transfer tax page gives the rate. Sellers or their closing office file the PT-61 declaration electronically.

For questions about whether a particular transfer is taxable, the state directs people to the Clerk of Superior Court in the county.

sections.h2: What should a Stonecrest seller line up before accepting an offer?
sections.html:
1. Gather the deed, the DeKalb parcel number and the most recent assessment notice.
  2. See whether a homestead exemption is on file and warn any buyer that it will lapse for them.
  3. Read the August bill and note which installments are settled.
  4. Request a payoff figure from your servicer and a lien search from the attorney handling the closing.
  5. Judge each offer by what you keep after transfer tax, repair credits and timing.

faqs.a: Yes. Voters created it on November 8, 2016 and it began operating on July 10, 2017. The city runs zoning, permits and business licenses, and DeKalb County bills property tax and handles public safety.

faqs.q: When are DeKalb County property tax installments due?
faqs.a: Installments fall on September 30 and November 15, and paying everything at once means doing it by September 30. Late payments draw a 5 percent penalty under strict postmark rules.

faqs.q: Does my DeKalb homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. The county's brochure says exemptions cannot be transferred, so a buyer applies separately and must satisfy the January 1 ownership and residency tests.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my DeKalb property value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the mailing date printed on the assessment notice. Deliver the appeal by hand or have it postmarked by then, because fax and email filings are refused.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the property tax bill after I sell in Stonecrest?
faqs.a: The closing statement answers that. DeKalb mails a bill to the January 1 owner and to the new owner, and it tells buyers to ask the closing attorney or escrow agent who owes it. Unpaid tax stays with the property.
